primaryText: Dogs are sitting on my lawn. All dogs are mammals. Therefore: Mammals are sitting on my lawn.
discourseSegments: Dogs are sitting on my lawn.
Therefore: Mammals are sitting on my lawn.
comment: The inference appears to be valid, as it would be with the indefinite plural an existential (p. 445).

primaryText: Dogs are good pets. All dogs are mammals. Therefore: Mammals are good pets.
comment: An invalid argument, a case of overgeneralization (p. 445). The second premise is printed without its period.

primaryText: Max believes some dogs are here.
comment: Exhibits a transparent reading, with 'some dogs' outside the scope of 'believes', (131') (p. 452); the opaque reading is the one (132) shares.
Has only the narrow scope reading: Max's belief has nothing to do with particular dogs (p. 452).

context: Read literally, of a world like ours, in which a particular individual can be in only one place at a time, and with dogs at every relevant place.
comment: Cannot receive a normal literal interpretation, though not ill-formed; a hyperbolic use is set aside (pp. 453-454).
